name: Place el-Hedim
hero_subtitle: The main square of imperial Meknes: Bab Mansour, cafés, carriages and the daily pulse of the medina.

overview.title: The living heart of Meknes
overview.p1: Place el-Hedim is the open square that faces Bab Mansour, the ceremonial gate of Meknes. By day it is a meeting point with horse carriages, snack stalls and a clear view of the monumental façade; by late afternoon the light softens and the square fills with locals and visitors.
overview.p2: Start here to orient yourself in the medina: Bab Mansour is the landmark, the Musée de Meknès sits on one side, and lanes lead toward the souks and the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail. The square itself is free and open; you can sit, walk the edges and watch the gate change colour with the sun.
overview.p3: Allow 30–60 minutes for photos, a mint tea and a first sense of Meknes. Combine it with Bab Mansour, then walk deeper into the medina or continue to the imperial quarter.

food.title: Snacks on the square
food.p1: Snack stalls and simple cafés line the edges of the square. Expect orange juice, grilled snacks and mint tea more than fine dining — keep it casual and watch the gate while you eat.
food.li5: Pay fairly and keep the square clear
food.p2: The square is busiest late afternoon; mornings are quieter for photos without crowds.

1.title: Light first, then walk
1.desc: Late afternoon gives the best colour on Bab Mansour. After photos, walk the perimeter of the square, then pick a lane into the medina or toward the mausoleum.

2.title: Use the square as a hub
2.desc: Place el-Hedim is the easiest place to meet a driver, start a guided walk or reset after the souks. Note landmarks on each side of the gate so you can find your way back.

3.title: Combine with Bab Mansour
3.desc: The gate and the square form one scene. Read the Bab Mansour page for architecture detail, then use this square for atmosphere and orientation.

q1.question: Is Place el-Hedim free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes. The square is a public space. You can walk, sit and photograph the exterior of Bab Mansour without a ticket.

q2.question: Best time of day for photos?
q2.answer: Late afternoon for warm light on Bab Mansour. Morning is quieter if you prefer fewer people.

q3.question: How long should I stay?
q3.answer: Thirty to sixty minutes is enough for most visitors; longer if you sit for tea or start a medina walk from here.

q4.question: Where can I eat on the square?
q4.answer: Simple stalls and cafés around the edges serve juice, snacks and tea. For a fuller meal, walk a few minutes into the medina.

q5.question: What should I combine with Place el-Hedim?
q5.answer: Bab Mansour first (or from the square), then the medina lanes, the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail, and optionally a half-day to Volubilis.
